statement: A water tank is three quarters full. After 12 litres are used, it is half full. How many litres does the tank hold when it is full?

choices.misconception: I took 1/2 from 3/4 by working out 3 - 1 and 4 - 2, which gives 2/2, so I thought 12 litres was the whole tank.
I thought the 12 litres used were three quarters of the tank.
I gave how much water is in the tank now that it is half full.
I gave how much water was in the tank at the start, when it was three quarters full.

hints: What fraction of the tank do the 12 litres make up?
Find the difference between three quarters and one half. That fraction of the tank is the 12 litres, so scale it up to the whole tank.
Three quarters minus one half is one quarter, so 12 litres is one quarter of the tank. The whole tank is four quarters.

solutions.reliable: The water level drops from 3/4 of the tank to 1/2 of the tank, which is a drop of 3/4 - 2/4 = 1/4 of the tank. That quarter is the 12 litres, so the full tank holds 4 × 12 = 48 litres. Check: 3/4 of 48 is 36, and 36 - 12 = 24, which is half of 48. The transferable idea: the change in a fraction matches the change in the amount.

whyOnTest: A fractions-of-a-quantity check: the given amount matches a difference of two fractions, not either fraction itself.
